title: HTML Forms (Production Template Test)
description: Every chunk is immediately followed by a quick 2-option check, Sololearn-style, before a bigger checkpoint quiz closes each section.

sections.title: What Is an HTML Form?

chunks.text: An HTML form lets users enter data and send it to a server.

check.question: A form's main job is to...

chunks.text: Forms are built using the <form> tag as a container for input fields.

check.question: True or false: `<form>` acts as a container that wraps input fields.

chunks.text: Every field inside it gets bundled together when the form is submitted.

check.question: When a form is submitted, its fields are...
options: Sent one at a time automatically

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of an HTML `<form>` element?
options: To collect input and send it to the server
To style the page using colors and fonts
To link one HTML page directly to another one
To display images without needing a URL

sections.lesson:
Checkpoint: What Is an HTML Form?
Quick recap before the checkpoint: forms collect input and send it to the server.

sections.title: Basic Form Elements

chunks.text: The <input> tag creates a field where users type or select data.

check.question: `<input>` is used to...
options: Create a field for user data

chunks.text: A <label> tag describes what an input is for, improving accessibility.

check.question: A `<label>` mainly helps...
options: Explain what an input field is for
Send the form to the server

chunks.text: Connecting a label to its input uses the `for` attribute matching the input's `id`.

check.question: True or false: the `for` attribute links a label to an input by matching its `id`.

quiz.question: Type the tag name used to describe what an input field is for.

sections.lesson:
Checkpoint: Basic Form Elements
Quick recap before the checkpoint: creates fields,

sections.title: Form Attributes: action & method

chunks.text: The `action` attribute tells the form where to send data when submitted.

check.question: The `action` attribute defines...
options: Where the form data is sent

chunks.text: The `method` attribute controls how data is sent — commonly `GET` or `POST`.

check.question: True or false: `method` can be set to GET or POST.

chunks.text: Together they answer: where does the data go, and how does it travel?

check.question: `action` and `method` together define...
options: Destination and transport of form data
The color scheme of the form

quiz.question: Arrange the tokens to build a form tag that submits to `save.php` using POST.

sections.lesson:
Checkpoint: Form Attributes: action & method
Quick recap before the checkpoint: action says where, method says how.

sections.title: Input Types

chunks.text: The `type` attribute of `<input>` changes how the field behaves.

check.question: True or false: `password` is a valid input type.

chunks.text: Browsers can validate some types automatically, like rejecting a badly formatted email.

check.question: Automatic browser validation happens for types like...

quiz.question: What extra behavior does using `type="email"` give this input, compared to `type="text"`?
options: The browser can check that the value looks valid
The field autofills using the user's saved email
The field turns read-only until JavaScript allows it
The field hides typed text the way passwords do

sections.lesson:
Checkpoint: Input Types
Quick recap before the checkpoint: the type attribute changes an input's behavior.

sections.title: Form Validation Attributes

chunks.text: The `required` attribute stops a form from submitting if the field is empty.
The `pattern` attribute checks input against a regular expression.

check.question: True or false: `pattern` uses a regular expression to validate input.

chunks.text: These checks happen in the browser, before any data reaches the server.

check.question: Browser-side validation happens...
options: Before data is sent to the server

quiz.question: Type the attribute name that makes a field mandatory before the form can submit.

sections.lesson:
Checkpoint: Form Validation Attributes
Quick recap before the checkpoint: required and pattern validate in the browser.

sections.title: Submitting Forms: GET vs POST

chunks.text: `GET` appends form data to the URL as a query string — visible and bookmarkable.

check.question: GET puts form data...
options: In the URL as a query string
In a hidden server log only

chunks.text: `POST` sends data in the request body — hidden from the URL, better for sensitive or large data.

check.question: True or false: POST data appears directly in the URL.

chunks.text: Choosing the right method matters for security and how the server receives data.

check.question: Method choice affects...
options: Security and how data is received

quiz.question: Arrange the tokens to build a form tag that submits using GET to `search.php`.

sections.lesson:
Checkpoint: Submitting Forms: GET vs POST
Quick recap before the checkpoint: GET shows data in the URL, POST hides it in the body.

objectives: Explain what an HTML form is and why it's used.
Identify the core form elements: <input> and <label>.
Configure a form's action and method attributes.
Choose appropriate input types for different kinds of data.
Apply validation attributes like required and pattern.
Compare GET and POST when submitting form data.
recap: Forms collect user input and send it to the server.
<input> creates fields; <label> describes them for accessibility.
action says where data goes; method says how it travels.
The type attribute changes how an input behaves and validates.
required and pattern validate input in the browser before submission.
GET exposes data in the URL; POST hides it in the request body.
